reviews.body:
Thanks a lot for tracking this down and for the clear repro in #9089. The fix does what it says: I ran the new test against main (it fails, `tool_calls` is `None`) and against this branch (it passes), and the reassembled calls match what `litellm.stream_chunk_builder` produces for the same chunks. A few things before the SDK team takes it:

1. `completion_chunks_aggregator.py:38-41`: the `index is None` fallback can't trigger, since LiteLLM's `ChatCompletionDeltaToolCall.index` is a required `int` (constructing one with `index=None` raises a ValidationError). If it ever did trigger, every unindexed first fragment would land on position 0 and separate calls would be concatenated into one. Please drop it, which also settles the unindexed-test thread.
2. Your #8995 adds `opik/integrations/_streamed_tool_calls.StreamedToolCalls` for exactly this merge, and it handles LiteLLM deltas as they are (I fed it the same fragments and got identical output). Two implementations of the same reassembly will drift, so whichever of the two lands first, the other should call `StreamedToolCalls` (`add` per delta tool call, `to_list()` at the end) instead of `_merge_tool_call_deltas`.
3. `test_completion_chunks_aggregator.py:62-69` and `:74-77`: please assert the whole aggregated message (`message.model_dump()` against an expected dict) instead of projecting `(id, name, arguments)` tuples or checking `content` alone, and use random ids, names and arguments rather than fixed literals.
4. Please also cover a stream with both text and a tool call, and a single call whose id and name arrive only on the first fragment, with the arguments spread over several chunks.

Minor:
5. `completion_chunks_aggregator.py:47`: `type` is hardcoded to `"function"`; taking it from the first fragment that carries it keeps parity with the non-streamed response.
6. A `tools=` + `stream=True` case in `tests/library_integration/litellm/test_litellm_streaming.py` asserting the span output via `SpanModel` would cover this through `track_completion`, like #8995 does for Groq, Together and Cerebras.
Thanks a lot for this, @pcbeingused333! The fix is solid and the tests cover it really well. We're almost there to merge, with just one small change left (see the inline comment).

We accept some duplication across integrations here, because each provider can change its format on its own.

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed review. Pushed in c25e71cc63:

1. Dropped the `index is None` fallback.
2. The aggregator now uses `StreamedToolCalls` (`add` per delta tool call, `to_list()` at the end); `_merge_tool_call_deltas` is gone. `_streamed_tool_calls.py` and its unit test are copied unchanged from #8995 (as in #8995 c1d681d08d), so the two PRs add an identical file and merge cleanly in either order.
3. The tests assert the whole aggregated message (`message.model_dump()` against an expected dict) with random ids, names and arguments.
4. Added a stream with both text and a tool call, and a single call whose id and name arrive only on the first fragment with the arguments spread over several chunks.
5. `type` now comes from the first fragment that carries it (the helper does this).

Not done: 6 (a `tools=` + `stream=True` case in `tests/library_integration/litellm/test_litellm_streaming.py`). Those tests call the live provider and need an API key that was not available here, so the span output through `track_completion` was not exercised end to end; the aggregator is covered with real LiteLLM chunk types instead. It can be added if someone with a key can run it.

The unindexed-case Baz comment no longer applies since that path is gone. The Baz comment about `+=` on the arguments now concerns the shared helper in #8995, not this PR.
Thanks for the thorough update. The shared helper and expanded aggregation coverage address the prior concerns; understood on the live-provider test constraint.

Thanks for the quick update, @pcbeingused333, and for moving to the shared `StreamedToolCalls` helper. Before we take another look, could you go through the open Baz threads? For each one, either push a change or reply with a short note if you think the current code is right:

- [Unindexed tool calls lack regression coverage](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/pull/9092#discussion_r4331417161)
- [Tool arguments incur quadratic assembly cost](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/pull/9092#discussion_r4331417171)
- [Tool-call output behavior lacks public documentation](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/pull/9092#discussion_r4331417179)
- [Tool arguments merge under truncated indices](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/pull/9092#discussion_r4334572020)
- [Streamed tool-call span output lacks integration test](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/pull/9092#discussion_r4334572030)
- [Unit test imports undeclared together package](https://github.com/comet-ml/opik/pull/9092#discussion_r4334572037)

Thanks again!

Thanks for the pointers. All six open threads now have a reply, and the code for each is in 0fdf596b8c (the head of this branch):

- Unindexed fallback: it now lives in `StreamedToolCalls` and is covered in `tests/unit/integrations/test_streamed_tool_calls.py`; a LiteLLM-level `index=None` case can't be built because the field is a required `int`.
- Quadratic argument assembly: `StreamedToolCalls` keeps the fragments in a list and joins them once in `to_list()`.
- Docstring: `aggregate()` documents the merge by `index`, the fallback by `id`, argument concatenation, ordering and text-only streams.
- Truncated indices: a non-integral index is treated as missing instead of being cast to `int`, with a regression test.
- Span output: `test_tracked_stream_tool_calls.py` streams a tool call through `track_completion` with LiteLLM's `mock_response` and asserts `choices[0].message.tool_calls` on the recorded span output. The live-provider case from your point 6 still needs an API key, so it is not included.
- `together` import: the unit test no longer imports it.

Merger   🟠 Needs Review

 Not ready to merge: PR has unresolved findings that need to be addressed.
Thanks a lot for your hard work on this, @pcbeingused333, and for sticking with it through the review rounds to get it over the line. Much appreciated!
